# Install items and handlers

This page is for developers who read or write the `<install>` part of a package, and for administrators who want to
know what an install will do to a site. It answers: what an install item is, which code runs it, and what each
handler changes.

## Install items

An install item is one `<item>` of the `<install>` list in `package.xml`:

```xml
<install>
  <item type="ezcontentclass" filename="class-article" sub-directory="ezcontentclass"/>
  <item type="ezcontentobject" filename="contentobjects" sub-directory="ezcontentobject"/>
  <item type="ezextension" filename="extension-ezwebin" sub-directory="ezextension"/>
  <item type="ezfile" collection="default"/>
</install>
```

`type` names the handler. `sub-directory` and `filename` name the item's document,
`<package>/<sub-directory>/<filename>.xml`. The `<uninstall>` list has the same form. Items run in the order they are
listed; `eZPackage::installUnaudited()` skips an item whose `type`, `filename` and `sub-directory` repeat an earlier
one.

## How a handler is found

`eZPackage::packageHandler( $type )` looks the type up in `settings/package.ini`:

```ini
[PackageSettings]
HandlerAlias[ezcontentclass]=eZContentClassPackageHandler
HandlerAlias[ezcontentobject]=eZContentObjectPackageHandler
HandlerAlias[eziniaddon]=eZINIAddonPackageHandler
HandlerAlias[ezfile]=eZFilePackageHandler
HandlerAlias[ezini]=eZFilePackageHandler
HandlerAlias[ezdesign]=eZFilePackageHandler
HandlerAlias[eztemplate]=eZFilePackageHandler
HandlerAlias[ezthumbnail]=eZFilePackageHandler
HandlerAlias[ezsql]=eZDBPackageHandler
HandlerAlias[ezextension]=eZExtensionPackageHandler
HandlerAlias[ezinstallscript]=eZInstallScriptPackageHandler
```

The class is created through `eZExtension::getHandlerClass()` and kept for the request. A type without an entry
has no handler: the install of that item fails with "No package handler found for install item type '...'". Because
this is an INI array, another handler can be registered with a further `HandlerAlias[<type>]=<class>` entry in an
override or an extension's `package.ini.append.php`; the class must extend `eZPackageHandler`
(`kernel/classes/ezpackagehandler.php`).

## The shipped handlers

| Item type | Handler | Folder | Install | Uninstall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ezcontentclass` | `eZContentClassPackageHandler` | `kernel/classes/packagehandlers/ezcontentclass/` | Creates the class from its document, with its attributes, in its class groups. An identifier that is taken gets `_1`, `_2` ... | Removes the class matched by remote ID, after a confirmation when objects of it exist |
| `ezcontentobject` | `eZContentObjectPackageHandler` | `.../ezcontentobject/` | Creates the objects listed in `contentobjects.xml` (`<object-files-list>`, one `object-<remote id>.xml` each) below the top nodes, then installs templates, overrides and fetch aliases the document carries | Removes the objects |
| `ezextension` | `eZExtensionPackageHandler` | `.../ezextension/` | Copies `<sub-directory>/<name>/` to `extension/<name>/`, regenerates the extension autoloads and adds the name to `ActiveExtensions[]` in `settings/override/site.ini.append.php` | Deletes `extension/<name>/`, removes it from `ActiveExtensions[]`, regenerates the autoloads |
| `ezfile`, `ezini`, `ezdesign`, `eztemplate`, `ezthumbnail` | `eZFilePackageHandler` | `.../ezfile/` | Copies every file of the item's `collection` to its place: `design/<design>/templates`, `images`, `stylesheets`, `fonts`; `settings/[override/][siteaccess/<name>/]`; or a plain path. Thumbnails are not copied. INI files can get variables set | from 6.0.15 on: removes the files its install created and nobody changed since (see the note below) |
| `ezsql` | `eZDBPackageHandler` | `.../ezdb/` | Runs `sql/[<database-type>/]<filename>` through `eZDB::insertFile()`; with a `database-type` of another engine than the current one the file is not run and the item returns failure | nothing: SQL cannot be reversed; the item counts as not uninstalled |
| `eziniaddon` | `eZINIAddonPackageHandler` | `.../eziniaddon/` | Writes INI blocks of a siteaccess, turning remote IDs into the IDs of this site | nothing: the blocks stay; the item counts as not uninstalled |
| `ezinstallscript` | `eZInstallScriptPackageHandler` | `.../ezinstallscript/` | Nothing: returns success. The script is run by a step installer (below) | nothing |

The files differ in what they read: `ezcontentclass`, `ezcontentobject`, `ezextension` and `eziniaddon` read the
item's document before `install()` is called (`extractInstallContent()`), the others do not.

> **Note**
> Before 6.0.15, `eZFilePackageHandler`, `eZDBPackageHandler` and `eZINIAddonPackageHandler` had no `uninstall()`
> of their own: the base method did nothing and returned no value, which `eZPackage::uninstall()` counted as an
> item that did not uninstall, and files, SQL and INI changes stayed on the site. From 6.0.15 on:
>
> - `eZFilePackageHandler::uninstall()` removes a file only when its install created it (it did not exist before;
>   the install remembers it in the install data as `installed_files`), its path is relative and inside the
>   installation, its content is unchanged since, and that content is one of the package's own files. Everything
>   else stays: a file the install replaced, a file the site changed, an INI file that got variables at install
>   time, and the directories. A package installed before 6.0.15 has nothing remembered, so nothing is removed.
> - `eZDBPackageHandler` and `eZINIAddonPackageHandler` have an `uninstall()` that changes nothing and says why in
>   the debug output: SQL cannot be reversed automatically, and INI blocks may hold the site's own values since.
>   The item still counts as not uninstalled; remove those changes by hand.

## What happens to one item

`eZPackage::installItem()` does this for every item:

1. Find the handler; fail when there is none.
2. When the handler extracts content, read `<sub-directory>/<filename>.xml` (or its `.json` twin); fail when it
   cannot be read.
3. Open a database transaction.
4. Call the handler's `install()` with the package, the item and the install parameters.
5. Commit on success; roll back when the handler returns false, leaves the transaction invalid, or throws.

The whole package fails at the first failing item unless the install parameters say `continue-on-error`. A package
whose items all succeeded is recorded as installed in the `ezpackage` table (name, `<number>-<release>`, date). What
the handlers remember for the uninstall is kept as install data (`<install-data>`).

## Conflicts: an item that meets something existing

Handlers report a conflict through `$installParameters['error']` with a code, a description and the actions a person
may choose. The administration's install page shows them; the choice can be remembered for the rest of the run.

| Handler | Conflict | Actions offered |
|---|---|---|
| `ezcontentclass` | A class with the same remote ID exists | Replace (with a warning about the objects that go with it), Update existing class (attributes added and updated, none removed), Skip, Keep existing and create a new one |
| `ezextension` | `extension/<name>/` exists | Replace extension, Skip |
| `ezextension` | The name is not a valid extension name | none: the item fails |

With `non-interactive` set, nobody can answer, so a handler takes its non-interactive branch:
`ezcontentclass` **skips** a class that exists ("Non-interactive installs (e.g. CLI) must not destructively replace
existing classes"), while `ezextension` **replaces** an existing extension directory.

## Handlers in the setup wizard and in ezpm

The Create sites step installs each required package with these parameters
(`kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_create_sites.php`):

```php
array( 'use_dates_from_package' => true,
       'site_access_map' => array( '*' => $userSiteaccessName ),
       'top_nodes_map' => array( '*' => 2 ),
       'design_map' => array( '*' => $userDesignName ),
       'language_map' => $languageMap,
       'restore_dates' => true,
       'user_id' => $user->attribute( 'contentobject_id' ),
       'non-interactive' => true );
```

`ezpm install` uses the same kind of map with the siteaccess of the run and top node 2 (or the destination node
given), also `non-interactive`. Both therefore skip classes that exist and replace extensions that exist.

## The step installers of the administration

Beside the handlers, `settings/package.ini [InstallerSettings]` names step installers for the administration's
install page:

```ini
[InstallerSettings]
HandlerList[]=ezcontentobject
HandlerList[]=ezinstallscript
HandlerAlias[ezcontentobject]=eZContentObjectPackageInstaller
HandlerAlias[ezinstallscript]=eZInstallScriptPackageInstaller
InstallBatchMaxItems=12
InstallBatchTimeBudgetSeconds=6
```

They live in `kernel/classes/packageinstallers/` and add pages to the install (for example, choosing where content
goes). `InstallBatchMaxItems` and `InstallBatchTimeBudgetSeconds` split a long install into batches; see
[package installer batching](../../../features/6.0/package-installer-batching.md).
